title: Immunohistochemistry for protein detection in PFA-fixed paraffin-embedded SARS-CoV-2-infected COPD airway epithelium
protocol: Coat 100 mm² cell culture dish with 5 mL PureCol for 20 min at 15°C–25°C.
Thaw cryopreserved primary early-passage (P0) NHBE cells in a water bath at 37°C.
Add 1 mL of new cAEC medium into the cryovial drop by drop using a sterile pipette.
Transfer cells from the cryovial into a 15 mL conical tube.
Spin the cells at 330 × g at 4°C for 5 min in a benchtop centrifuge.
Remove supernatant and resuspend cell pellet in 2 mL of cAEC medium.
Add cell solution to the precoated 100 mm dish containing 8 mL of cAEC medium, swirling gently for homogeneous distribution.
Incubate cells at 37°C and 5% CO₂.
Replace cAEC medium every 48 hours.
Once cells are fully confluent (around 90%), split the cells at a 1 in 3 ratio.
Remove old-medium from confluent NHBE culture in a 100 mm dish.
Wash with 5 mL of sterile 1× DPBS.
Add 5 mL of TrypLE express and incubate for 5 min at 37°C.
Transfer the cells into a 15 mL conical tube.
Spin at 330 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in cAEC medium.
Seed cells into a new 100 mm dish at a desired cell concentration using a 1:3 ratio for subculture.
Coat Transwells (e.g., 6.5 mm) at the apical side with 100 μL PureCol for 20 minutes at 15°C–25°C.
Remove the old medium from a confluent NHBE culture in a 100 mm dish and wash with 5 mL of sterile 1× DPBS.
Add 5 mL of TrypLE express and incubate for 5 minutes at 37°C.
Transfer the cells into a 15 mL conical tube.
Spin at 330 × g for 5 minutes at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 2 mL of cAEC medium.
Count the cells using trypan blue dye and hematocytometer.
Seed 50,000 cells in 100 μL of cAEC medium on the apical side of a Transwell.
Add 500 μL of cAEC medium on the basal side.
Remove cAEC medium from both apical and basal sides of the Transwell.
Add 500 μL complete PneumaCult-ALI medium on the basal side of the Transwell.
Replace complete PneumaCult-ALI medium every 48 hours on basal sides for differentiation for 3–4 weeks.
Wash mucus with 200 μL sterile 1× DPBS once a week starting from day 14 of differentiation.
Increase mucus washing frequency to every other day when excessive mucus production is observed.
Verify airway epithelium Ciliary function by quantifying ciliary beat frequency (CBF) using high-speed live-cell imaging followed by image quantification using SAVA-system.
Measure transepithelial electrical resistance (TEER) using an EVOM2 voltmeter for membrane integrity verification.
PFA-fixate SARS-CoV-2 infected COPD airway epithelium.
Paraffin-embed and section PFA-fixed samples.
Stain sections for SARS-CoV-2 S or N.
Infect four-week differentiated COPD epithelium in Transwells with SARS-CoV-2 (nCoV-WA1–2020) at an MOI of 0.1 for four days at 37°C.
Wash apical and basal sides of the Transwells twice with 1× DPBS (200 μL for apical, 500 μL for basal).
Add freshly prepared 4% paraformaldehyde solution to both apical and basal sides of the Transwells (200 μL for apical, 500 μL for basal).
Incubate the Transwells at 15°C–25°C for 18–24 hours.
Remove PFA and wash the Transwells twice with 1× DPBS on both sides (200 μL for apical, 500 μL for basal).
Submerge Transwells in 1× DPBS for storage at 4°C.
Take out polycarbonate membrane containing the epithelium from the Transwell using a sterile scalpel.
Place the membrane in a petri dish containing PBS.
Cut the membrane into at least two small pieces to fit into a Paraffin cassette.
Place the membrane into a Paraffin cassette containing PBS.
Incubate the membrane in paraffin for three 30-min steps in a vacuum oven set at 58°C +/− 2°C under pressure.
Embed the membrane on the edge of the paraffin block and store the block at 4°C.
Cut sections about 5 μm thick using a rotary microtome and mount onto superfrost plus slides.
Store sectioned slides at 4°C for several months.
Deparaffinize membrane on section slides by incubating them in specified solutions.
Transfer slides into a slide chamber and submerge them in R-Buffer A 10× solution.
Fill the 2100 Retriever’s body with 750 mL of deionized water.
Place the slide chamber rack into the body.
Secure the lid and close the depressurizing valve.
Push the Start button and run for 20 min.
Let the unit cool down for 2 h or longer at 15°C–25°C.
Remove slide chambers from 2100 Retriever after cooling.
Place slides in a coplin jar.
Wash slides 3 times for 10-min each in 1× PBST.
Incubate the coplin jar on a belly button shaker at medium speed for efficient washing.
After final wash, gently wick away as much PBS as possible using a fresh KimWipe without disturbing the tissue.
Draw a circle around each tissue with a PAP pen to create a hydrophobic barrier.
Add 300 ul of blocking buffer (10% goat serum in 1× PBS) around each tissue section.
Incubate slides at 15°C–25°C for 2 h in a humidified, light-protected chamber.
Prepare solution for primary antibody incubation in antibody diluent (10% goat serum in 1× PBS).
Mix SARS-CoV-2 N specific mouse monoclonal at a 1:10 dilution with Acetyl-alpha-tubulin specific rabbit polyclonal at a 1:500 dilution.
Mix SARS-CoV-2 S specific rabbit polyclonal at a 1:100 dilution with specific mouse monoclonal p63 at a 1:100 dilution.
Remove blocking buffer by gently wicking away with a KimWipe.
Add 100 μL of primary antibody solution to the slides.
Incubate the slides for around 12 hours at 4°C in a humidified light-protectant chamber.
Do not allow tissue to dry out during incubation.
Remove primary antibody solution from the slides after incubation.
Wash the slides three times with 1× PBST.
Prepare secondary antibody solution (goat anti-mouse AF488 and goat anti-rabbit AF647) at a 1:100 dilution in antibody diluent.
Alternatively, prepare secondary antibody solution (goat anti-rabbit AF647 and goat anti-mouse AF488) at a 1:100 dilution in antibody diluent.
Gently wick away as much PBS as possible from each section using a fresh KimWipe.
Add 100 μL of the appropriate secondary antibody solution to each section.
Incubate slides in secondary antibody solution for 45 min at 15°C–25°C in a humidified, light-protected chamber.
Perform three 10-min washes with PBST in a coplin jar and on the shaker.
Prepare rhodamine phalloidin solution 1:100 in antibody diluent (PBS with 10% goat serum).
Wipe each slide with a KimWipe to remove excess liquid.
Add 100 μL of rhodamine phalloidin solution to each section and incubate for 30 min at 15°C–25°C in a humidified, light-protected chamber.
Perform three 10-min washes with PBST in a coplin jar using a shaker.
Add one drop of DAPI (NucBlue TM fixed cell stain ReadyProbes) to each slide.
Incubate for 5 min at 15°C–25°C in a humidified, light-protected chamber.
Perform two 10-min washes with PBST in a coplin jar using a shaker.
Add one water wash for 10 min.
After the final wash, mount each slide with a coverslip using gold antifade reagent.
Add all channels on the software.
Set DAPI channel with excitation (EX) at 325–375 nm and emission (EM) at 435–485 nm.
Set Phalloidin channel with EX at 540–580 nm and EM at 592–668 nm.
Set AF488 channel with EX at 460–500 nm and EM at 512–542 nm.
Set AF647 channel with EX at 590–650 nm and EM at 662–738 nm.
Find the membrane section using a 5× objective.
Take images of the membrane section using a 63× oil objective for higher resolution.
Process acquired images using 2D- or 3D-deconvolution in LASX software to enhance image sharpness.
